l: BERGEN: A Benchmarking Library for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, BERGEN: A Benchmarking Library for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, B
s: The unit analyzes whether ELI5 and WoW are suitable for RAG evaluation in the benchmark, using different retrievers and SOLAR 10.7B and Llama2 70B. On ELI5, the Closed Book setting outperforms Oracle retrieval, while retrievers have low retrieval performance but sometimes improve generation quality relative to Oracle. On WoW, the Closed Book setting also outperforms retrieval-based systems, and it is unclear why the dialogue task should depend on Wikipedia knowledge. NQ is presented as a suitable RAG dataset because stronger retrieval systems produce increasing benefits and Oracle retrieval achieves the highest performance.

l: BERGEN: A Benchmarking Library for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, BERGEN: A Benchmarking Library for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, H
s: This unit describes BERGEN’s support for multilingual retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) across 12 non-English languages, including multilingual retrieval, generation, datasets, datastores, metrics, and results. BGE-M3 is used for dense multilingual retrieval and BGE-reranker-v2-m3 is identified as the reranker, while Command-R-35B serves as the multilingual generator. Experiments use MKQA and XOR-TyDi QA with English, user-language, concatenated, and all-language Wikipedia datastores. Results show that multilingual Wikipedia retrieval is beneficial in most cases, that the best datastore depends on the dataset, and that character 3-gram recall is more robust than word-level matching for transliterations.

l: Unsupervised Information Refinement Training of Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Unsupervised Information Refinement Training of Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: The unit examines retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and the difficulty large language models (LLMs) have in effectively using retrieved information. It proposes viewing LLMs as an “Information Refiner” that integrates retrieved knowledge with model parameters to produce more concise, accurate, and complete text. The authors introduce INFO-RAG, an unsupervised, low-cost, and general information-refinement training method for RAG. Across 11 diverse datasets, INFO-RAG improves LLaMA2’s zero-shot performance by an average of 9.39% relative points and improves in-context learning and RAG robustness.

s: Retrieved information can be incorrect, incomplete, or not useful, and large language models may still fail to use it effectively. INFO-RAG is designed to help models consistently integrate this information with their stored knowledge.

s: Retrieved texts vary in correctness, completeness, and usefulness, and language models may ignore or be misled by them. The proposed Information Refiner perspective aims to transform them into text that is more concise, accurate, and complete.

l: Information Refiner, Unsupervised Information Refinement Training of Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: The Information Refiner is the proposed role of a large language model in RAG. In this role, the model integrates knowledge from retrieved texts and its parameters to generate text that is more concise, accurate, and complete than the retrieved texts.

s: The unit concerns retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and the difficulty large language models (LLMs) have in using retrieved texts of varying quality. s: Retrieval-augmented generation equips neural systems and large language models with retrieved information for generation tasks such as open-domain question answering and dialogue. l: Large Language Models, Unsupervised Information Refinement Training of Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Introduction
s: Large language models are used in RAG to provide additional knowledge and help mitigate hallucination, but their pre-training does not explicitly teach them to use retrieved texts as references. s: The unit proposes considering large language models as an “Information Refiner” in RAG. In this role, they generate text that is more concise, accurate, and complete than the input retrieved texts by combining retrieved knowledge with knowledge in their parameters.

l: RAG-Studio: Towards In-Domain Adaptation of Retrieval Augmented Generation Through Self-Alignment, RAG-Studio: Towards In-Domain Adaptation of Retrieval Augmented Generation Through Self-Alignment, Abstract
s: The abstract introduces RAG-Studio, a self-aligned training framework for adapting general Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems to specialized domains. RAG-Studio uses a specialized domain corpus to identify useful domain knowledge and synthesize training data. It then jointly fine-tunes the retriever and LLM within the RAG system so that retrieval becomes more precise and retrieved information is used more effectively. Experiments on Biomedical, Finance, Law, Computation, and Wiki domain-specific QA datasets show substantial improvements over generally trained RAG.
